services.title: Tumour immunology

services.title: Regulation of immune responses

aboutpara: I work in [Mo Lotfollahi's group](https://lotfollahi.com/) at the [Wellcome Sanger Institute](https://www.sanger.ac.uk/group/lotfollahi-group/), where **machine learning** meets **single-cell and spatial genomics**, developing methods to understand how **tissue context shapes cell states**, with a focus on the **tumour microenvironment** in **clear cell renal cell carcinoma** and **pancreatic cancer**. I trained in biotechnology at the **University of Pavia** and in systems biology at **ETH Zurich**, and did my PhD at the **University of Turin** and [SR-TIGET](https://research.hsr.it/en/institutes/san-raffaele-telethon-institute-for-gene-therapy/genomics-of-the-innate-immune-system/carlo-leonardi.html), working on **tumour-associated macrophages** in pancreatic cancer.
ambitions: I aim to develop **machine learning approaches** that are genuinely meaningful for **immunology and oncology**: models that **predict cell states and cell function**, and **patient embeddings** that support **patient stratification** in oncology. I'm driven by learning patterns from data, from **gene programmes** to **molecular and immune circuits**, and turning them into an understanding of **tissues, immunity and disease**. I pursue this in **academia**, through my own research, and with **industry**, through **collaborations and consultancy**.

resume.tagline: 👋 Computational biologist at the interface of machine learning and spatial genomics.
resume.description: I develop and apply machine learning methods to single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data, with a particular interest in macrophages, the tumour microenvironment and immunotherapy response.

experiences.position: Postdoctoral Researcher, Wellcome Sanger Institute (Lotfollahi lab)

experiences.position: Research Fellow in Bioinformatics and AI, Centro Cardiologico Monzino (Milan)

education.universityPara: Doctoral research on tumour-associated macrophages in Renato Ostuni's lab (SR-TIGET, Milan) and Claudio Isella's lab (Candiolo Cancer Institute, Turin). Previously: MSc in Biology, major in Systems Biology (ETH Zurich) and BSc in Biotechnology (University of Pavia).

collaborate.title: Let's work together
collaborate.intro: I'm always happy to hear from people interested in tumour immunology, spatial biology and machine learning, whether you're a clinician with a question, a fellow researcher or a student.

sections.heading: Research interests
sections.body: Tumour immunology and the tumour microenvironment, especially how spatial organisation and myeloid–lymphoid crosstalk shape immunotherapy response. Oncology across cancer types, including renal and pancreatic cancer. Macrophage biology across tissues. Machine learning methods for single-cell and spatial omics.

sections.heading: Collaborations
sections.body: I'm keen to collaborate with clinicians and experimental groups who have well-annotated tissue cohorts or clinical questions that spatial and single-cell data could answer, and with method developers interested in biological applications.

sections.heading: Students
sections.body: I host Master's and undergraduate students for research projects at the intersection of machine learning and biology. If you're interested, email me with a short note about your background and what you'd like to work on.

sections.heading: Get in touch
sections.body: Email is the best way to reach me. You can also find my publications on Google Scholar and my code on GitHub.
